title: Learning assets for at / on / in

classification.reason: At, on, and in are core English prepositions used to locate events or objects in time and space. B1 learners need to choose among them by judging how specific or broad the time or place is.

explanation.myUnderstanding: Use at for a precise point, such as a clock time or a specific place: at 7:30, at the station. Use on for a surface or a calendar day/date: on the wall, on Monday, on May 5. Use in for an enclosed or larger space and for longer time periods: in my bag, in China, in May, in 2026, in the morning.

similarities: All three often appear before nouns or noun phrases.
differences: At usually points to an exact time or a specific point-like location.
On usually points to a day/date or contact with a surface.
In usually points to a longer time period or being inside an area, container, or space.

association.note: Teach these as useful chunks first, then connect them to the general rule of point, surface/day, and area/period.

example.translation: This lesson starts at eight twenty.
example.note: Use at with an exact clock time.

example.english: We have a science test on Thursday.
example.translation: We have a science test on Thursday.
example.note: Use on with a weekday or a date.
Use in with years, months, seasons, and broad parts of the day.

example.english: Meet me at the library. I will be in the reading room.
example.translation: Meet me at the library. I will be in the reading room.
example.note: At the library treats the library as a meeting point; in the reading room focuses on being inside a room.

counterExample.reason: Use at 6:45 because 6:45 is an exact clock time. The correct sentence is: The train leaves at 6:45.
Use on April 12 because a full date is treated like a calendar day. The correct sentence is: Her birthday is on April 12.

assets.title: On the bus vs in the bus

confusion.confusedWith: on the bus and in the bus
confusion.reason: On the bus is the normal phrase when someone is using a bus as transport. In the bus focuses on the physical inside of the vehicle, often when talking about an object or location inside it.

scenario.description: A student describes a normal school day: arrive at school at 7:40, have art on Wednesday, eat lunch in the classroom on rainy days, and play basketball in the gym after school.

conversation.speaker: Leo
conversation.text: Yes. Let's meet at the sports center at 3:00.

conversation.speaker: Mia
conversation.text: Good idea. We can play basketball in the gym.

conversation.speaker: Leo
conversation.text: Great. I'll put my water bottle in my bag now.

mnemonic.content: Think of at as a point, on as a surface or calendar square, and in as a box or larger period.

production.mySentence: Write three sentences about your week: one with at, one with on, and one with in.
production.feedback: Check that at is used for an exact time or point, on for a day/date or surface, and in for a longer period or inside space.
